title: Responsive Web Design
description: Learn how to build layouts that work on any screen size.

pages.content: Responsive web design lets a webpage adapt to different screen sizes, from phones to desktops. One flexible layout works everywhere instead of separate sites per device. It matters because people visit pages on screens of many sizes.

Mobile-first design means designing for small screens first, then enhancing the layout for larger screens. Start with simple base styles for phones, then add min-width media queries as the screen grows.
The viewport meta tag controls how a page is scaled and displayed on different devices. Without it, mobile browsers may show a tiny, zoomed-out desktop layout. Place it in the head of your HTML.
width=device-width matches the page width to the device's CSS width, not a fixed number like 1000 pixels. initial-scale=1.0 sets the starting zoom to 100%. Together they make pages fit the screen.

quiz.question: What does responsive design allow a webpage to do?

choices: Designing for small screens first, then enhancing for larger screens
Testing mobile devices after desktop devices

quiz.question: What is the purpose of the viewport meta tag?
choices: To add animations to a webpage
To control how the page is displayed on different devices

pages.content: A media query is a CSS mechanism that applies rules only when certain conditions are met, such as a minimum or maximum screen width. One stylesheet can then give different styles to different screens.

Media queries can change layouts, font sizes, spacing, and other CSS properties. A breakpoint is a screen width or condition where responsive styles can change. Common breakpoints are around 480px, 768px, and 1024px.
min-width: 768px applies styles when the viewport is at least 768 pixels wide. max-width: 768px applies them when it is at most 768 pixels wide. Mobile-first designs mostly use min-width.
(width: 768px) matches only a viewport of exactly 768 pixels, so it is rarely useful. Names such as screen-width or screen with a size are not valid media features. Use min-width or max-width.

quiz.question: What is a media query used for?
choices: Applying CSS styles based on certain conditions

quiz.question: What does a breakpoint represent in responsive design?
choices: A screen width where the layout or styles can change

quiz.question: Which media query applies styles when the viewport is at least 768 pixels wide?

pages.content: Flexbox arranges items mainly along a single direction: a row or a column. Enable it with display: flex;. It suits navigation bars, button rows, and lists of cards.
justify-content distributes space between items along the main axis. align-items controls alignment on the cross axis. flex-direction switches between row and column.
CSS Grid arranges items in two dimensions, using rows and columns at the same time. Enable it with display: grid;. It suits page layouts and galleries.
grid-template-columns defines the columns of a Grid. The fr unit shares available space in fractions, so repeat(3, 1fr) creates three equal columns.
Relative units such as %, em, rem, vw, and vh scale more flexibly than fixed pixels. The vw unit is relative to the viewport width, and vh to the viewport height.
The rem unit is relative to the root element's font size. The em unit is relative to the font size of the relevant element or inherited context. Both help text and spacing scale smoothly.

Effective responsive layouts combine mobile-first design, media queries, Flexbox or Grid, and relative units. Avoid only fixed pixel widths and desktop-only styles so layouts adapt across screen sizes.
